characteristic_features: erythrocytosis (Hgb >16.5 g/dL men, >16.0 g/dL women, or Hct >49% men, >48% women)
key_complications: progression to post-PV myelofibrosis or AML

biomarkers.name: JAK2 V617F
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnostic. Higher allele burden has been associated with increased risk of thrombosis and disease progression in some studies

biomarkers.name: JAK2 exon 12
biomarkers.prevalence: ~2–5% overall; enriched in JAK2 V617F-negative PV
biomarkers.clinical_use: Alternative JAK2 mutation; often presents with predominant erythrocytosis

biomarkers.name: Serum erythropoietin (EPO)
biomarkers.prevalence: Low or subnormal in PV (distinguishes from secondary erythrocytosis)

biomarkers.name: ASXL1, SRSF2, IDH1/2 (high-risk mutations — HMR)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Adverse prognostic; increased risk of progression to myelofibrosis / AML and inferior survival

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Marrow panmyelosis — hypercellular marrow with proliferation of all three lineages (erythroid, granulocytic, megakaryocytic); pleomorphic mature megakaryocytes
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Not graded; IPSS-PV / MIPSS-PV for prognosis

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: JAK-STAT hyperactivation drives inflammatory cytokine production and constitutional symptoms
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Hypercellular marrow with panmyelosis; pleomorphic mature megakaryocytes

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: HSC with JAK2 mutation driving trilineage myeloproliferation
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Panmyelosis — hypercellular marrow with proliferation of all three lineages (erythroid, granulocytic, megakaryocytic); pleomorphic mature megakaryocytes; retained maturation with expanded output
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: JAK2 V617F (or exon 12 mutations) drives constitutive JAK-STAT signalling from the HSC through committed progenitors — explaining multilineage involvement; progression to post-PV myelofibrosis or AML represents clonal evolution with additional mutations
